title: Ukrainian forces enter Kherson after Russian withdrawal
body:
On 9 November 2022, Russian General Sergey Surovikin announced the withdrawal of Russian troops from Kherson and the right bank of the Dnipro, citing supply problems and Ukrainian shelling that endangered civilians. Russia's Defence Ministry said that all of roughly 30,000 soldiers and their equipment crossed to the left bank in an orderly way, though analysts doubted this and many reports described a chaotic withdrawal.

Ukrainian forces entered Kherson city on 11 November 2022 and took the rest of the right bank of Kherson Oblast and parts of Mykolaiv Oblast. They advanced cautiously because of mines and booby traps, which wounded several people and killed at least one. Residents gathered in Freedom Square to cheer the troops. President Volodymyr Zelensky made an unannounced visit on 14 November.

Russia ceded about 40 percent of Kherson Oblast. At least seven bridges had been destroyed, four of them over the Dnipro, and electricity, water and internet networks were largely down. Kherson had about 300,000 residents before the war and about 80,000 at the end of the occupation. In late October Russia had evacuated at least 70,000 civilians to the left bank, which Ukraine called deportations. Russia named Henichesk its temporary regional capital.
